group.passage:
In 2002, Thomas Hertog received an email inviting him to Stephen Hawking’s office. The young scientist rushed to Hawking’s Cambridge apartment, where he found Hawking’s eyes gleaming with joy. By typing on a computer-controlled speech system, Hawking told Hertog that he had changed his mind about the viewpoint from which his best-selling book, A Brief History of Time, was written.
[[1]] These conditions include a precise balance of particle forces that enable the existence of chemistry and complex molecules, as well as the presence of only three dimensions of space that makes possible the formation of stable solar systems and habitats for living organisms. [[2]]
Hertog and Hawking worked together for the next 20 years to create a new theory of the cosmos that could more adequately explain the genesis of life. [[3]] Eventually, their “conversations” led to Hawking’s ultimate idea, which served as the foundation for the book On the Origin of Time.
On the Origin of Time addresses the issue of our location in the cosmos and what makes our universe suitable for life. [[4]] This perspective provides a fresh insight into the fundamental purpose of cosmology and results in a new philosophy of physics which rejects the notion that the universe is a machine governed by unchanging laws with a prior existence. In a nutshell, their collaborative book offers a striking new outlook of the universe’s birth.

options_bank.A: Hertog explains that their new perspective reverses the order of laws and reality in physics.
options_bank.B: Hawking’s change of heart stemmed from his inability to grasp how the universe could create conditions ideal for life.
options_bank.C: Though Hawking’s disease paralyzed him and limited his ability to communicate, the collaboration was outstanding.
options_bank.D: Hawking declared that it was written from the wrong perspective, and the project was abandoned.
options_bank.E: It is believed that without these specific circumstances, life may not have developed in the universe.

tags.topic: Stephen Hawking and Thomas Hertog’s new theory of the origin of the universe
